overall: The Board's executive session topic was proper, and no deliberation or accessibility violation was found, but it violated the Law by skipping required procedural statements and omitting "open session" from its notice.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board convened in executive session for an improper purpose, namely its legal strategy on AAB and MCAD complaints.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, it was appropriate for the Board to convene in executive session under Purpose 3 to discuss its legal strategy with respect to complaints against the Board pending before these agencies.

allegations.summary: Board convened in executive session without stating specific litigation matters and without the chair's Purpose 3 detrimental-effect declaration.
allegations.key_passage: The Board's announcement prior to convening in executive session should have included information about the specific litigation matters it planned to discuss.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session was held in an inaccessible location, the Authority office in the building basement.
allegations.key_passage: there is no requirement that the executive session itself, which is closed to the public, also be held in an accessible location.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the meeting notice failed to list open session as a topic.
allegations.key_passage: listing "open session" on the meeting notice is the only means by which members of the public are informed that a public body will, in fact, hold an open meeting that they are permitted to attend.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged business was conducted outside a meeting when the chair, a member and the director signed checks right after the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: because only two of these three individuals are Board members.

allegations.summary: Board responded to the complaint through its executive director without first having the full Board review it.
allegations.key_passage: the Open Meeting Law and the Attorney General's regulations require that the entire public body first review the Open Meeting Law complaint.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
The Board may not rely on the Open Meeting Law to withhold the October 20, 2014 executive session minutes, though privilege or Public Records Law exemptions may still apply.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that future similar violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
